title: Le réveil du printemps
oneGoal: Students will observe and document spring changes in their environment
decisionPoints: Are students noticing seasonal changes?
What spring elements capture their attention?
How to connect observation to artistic potential?
progression: Foundation lesson - establishes connection between seasons and artistic inspiration
realWorldConnection: Noticing buds on trees, new flowers, changing weather, animals returning

title: Collection de trésors naturels
oneGoal: Students will ethically collect natural materials for art-making
decisionPoints: Are students collecting respectfully?
What materials are most inspiring to them?
How to balance collection with conservation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by actively gathering materials from observed environment
realWorldConnection: Finding interesting leaves, stones, twigs in their yard or neighborhood

title: Art éphémère dehors
oneGoal: Students will create temporary art installations outdoors
decisionPoints: Are students comfortable with temporary art?
What arrangements feel natural to them?
How to document without disrupting creation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by using collected materials in temporary compositions
realWorldConnection: Making patterns with sidewalk chalk that rain will wash away

title: Land art miniature
oneGoal: Students will create small-scale land art using natural materials
decisionPoints: Can students work at small scale effectively?
What patterns are they naturally drawn to?
How to encourage both planning and spontaneity?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by focusing on intentional design within nature
realWorldConnection: Arranging shells at the beach, making fairy circles with acorns

title: Couleurs de printemps
oneGoal: Students will match and recreate spring colors in their art
decisionPoints: Are students seeing subtle color variations?
What spring colors excite them most?
How to mix colors that match nature?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by adding color study to environmental observation
realWorldConnection: Noticing new green grass, pink blossoms, purple crocuses

title: Textures naturelles
oneGoal: Students will explore and recreate natural textures in their artwork
decisionPoints: Are students making texture connections?
What textures fascinate them most?
How to transfer natural textures to paper?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by adding tactile exploration to visual study
realWorldConnection: Feeling tree bark, smooth stones, soft moss, prickly pine cones

title: Empreintes de nature
oneGoal: Students will make prints and rubbings from natural objects
decisionPoints: Can students apply appropriate pressure for rubbings?
What objects make the clearest prints?
How to layer multiple textures effectively?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by creating permanent records of natural textures
realWorldConnection: Making leaf rubbings like they might do on nature walks with family

title: Jardin artistique
oneGoal: Students will design and create a small artistic garden space
decisionPoints: Are students thinking about long-term growth?
What aesthetic choices are they making?
How to balance artistic vision with plant needs?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by creating living art that changes over time
realWorldConnection: Helping with family garden, choosing flowers for beauty and growth

title: Mobile de printemps
oneGoal: Students will create hanging mobiles using collected natural materials
decisionPoints: Are students understanding balance concepts?
How do they respond to movement in art?
What natural materials work best for hanging?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by adding movement and spatial dimension to nature art
realWorldConnection: Wind chimes on porches, things hanging from trees in wind

title: Photographie nature
oneGoal: Students will document nature art through simple photography techniques
decisionPoints: Can students handle cameras/tablets appropriately?
What angles are they naturally choosing?
How to help them see light and shadow?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by learning to document and share environmental art
realWorldConnection: Taking pictures of their gardens, pets, special places outdoors

title: Art avec les saisons
oneGoal: Students will plan art projects that change with seasonal cycles
decisionPoints: Do students understand seasonal cycles?
What changes do they want to track?
How to plan for long-term observation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by thinking beyond immediate creation to cyclical processes
realWorldConnection: Watching their planted gardens grow, trees change through year

title: Installation collaborative
oneGoal: Students will work together to create a large environmental art installation
decisionPoints: How are students sharing ideas and materials?
What roles are emerging naturally?
How to ensure everyone contributes meaningfully?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by combining individual skills in collaborative creation
realWorldConnection: Working with neighbors on community gardens, school beautification

title: Respect pour l'environnement
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate understanding of environmental responsibility in art
decisionPoints: Are students making responsible choices?
How do they balance art-making with conservation?
What environmental connections are they making?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by emphasizing ethical relationship with natural materials
realWorldConnection: Leaving nature spaces better than they found them

title: Art et météo
oneGoal: Students will create art that responds to or incorporates weather conditions
decisionPoints: How are students adapting to weather conditions?
What weather elements inspire them most?
How to work safely in different weather?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by working with rather than against environmental conditions
realWorldConnection: Puddle jumping, shadow play, flying kites, catching snowflakes

title: Expo nature printemps
oneGoal: Students will curate and present their environmental art collection
decisionPoints: How do students choose work to display?
What stories are they telling about their art?
How comfortable are they sharing with others?
progression: Culminates all learning by presenting environmental art journey to community
realWorldConnection: Sharing nature discoveries with family, creating outdoor displays
